paper.title: Provably Optimal Algorithms for Generalized Linear Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic K-armed generalized linear contextual bandit
unmapped: K feature vectors per round drawn i.i.d. from unknown distribution nu with lambda_min(E[(1/K) sum_a x x']) >= sigma_0^2
Assumption 1: kappa = inf over ||x||<=1, ||theta-theta*||<=1 of mu'(x'theta) > 0 (local lower bound on link derivative)
Assumption 2: mu twice differentiable with mu' <= L_mu and mu'' <= M_mu
UCB-GLM tuning of tau requires knowledge of sigma_0
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, the agent observes a context consisting of a set of $K$ feature vectors, $\{x_{t,a} \mid a\in[K]\} \subset \R^d$, which is drawn IID from an unknown distribution $\nu$, with $\norm{x_{t,a}} \le 1$. Each feature vector $x_{t,a}$ is associated with an unknown stochastic reward $y_{t,a} \in [0,1]$. ... $\E[Y \mid X] = \mu(X'\theta^*)$ ... the noise $\epsilon_t$ is sub-Gaussian with parameter $\sigma$

symbols.C_univ: universal constant in tau = C sigma_0^{-2}(d+log(1/delta))
symbols.sigma_0: lower bound on sqrt of min eigenvalue of average context covariance

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: Fix any $\delta>0$. There exists a universal constant $C>0$, such that if we run UCB-GLM with $\alpha=\frac{\sigma}{\kappa} \sqrt{\frac{d}{2} \log(1+2T/d) + \log(1/\delta)}$ and $\tau=C\sigma_0^{-2}(d+\log(1/\delta))$, then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the regret of the algorithm is upper bounded by $R_T \le \tau + \frac{2 L_{\mu} \sigma d}{\kappa} \log ( \frac{T}{d\delta}) \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Probability 1-2delta. kappa mapped to c_mu (local version), L_mu mapped to k_mu. tau substituted into the bound. Paper notes delta=1/T gives E[R_T]=O~(d sqrt T).

conditions: T >= T_0 with T_0 = Omega(sigma^2/kappa^4 max{d^3, log(TK/delta)/d})

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For any $0 < \delta < 1$, if we run the SupCB-GLM algorithm with $\tau=\sqrt{dT}$ and $\alpha=\frac{3\sigma}{\kappa} \sqrt{2\log(TK/\delta)}$ for $T \ge T_0$ rounds, ... the regret of the algorithm is bounded as $R_T \le 45 (\sigma L_{\mu}/\kappa) \sqrt{\log T \log(TK/\delta)\log(T/d)} \sqrt{dT}$, with probability at least $1-\delta$.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: With $\delta = 1/T$, we obtain \[ \E[R_T] = O\left ((\log T)^{1.5} \sqrt{dT \log K} \right). \]

results.notes: R_T defined via mean rewards mu(x'theta*), so expectation is pseudo-regret.

bound.regime: T = Omega(sigma R d log^2 T/(kappa L_mu))

conditions: sum_{t=tau+1}^T lambda_min(V_t)^{-1/2} <= c sqrt(T) with probability at least 1-delta (condition on the algorithm's design matrices)
T = Omega((sigma R/(kappa L_mu)) d log^2 T)

source.label: thm:maindis
source.quote: We run algorithm UCB-GLM with $\tau=\frac{8\sigma^2}{\kappa^2}d\log T$ and $\alpha \le L_{\mu} \sigma/\kappa$. For any $\delta \in [1/T,1)$, suppose there is an universal constant $c$ such that $\sum_{t=\tau+1}^{T} \lmin^{-1/2}(V_t) \le c \sqrt{T}$ holds with probability at least $1-\delta$, and $T=\Omega(\frac{\sigma R}{ \kappa L_{\mu} } d \log^2 T)$. Then, the regret of the algorithm is bounded by $R_T \le \frac{C L_{\mu} \sigma}{\kappa} \sqrt{dT\log(T/\delta)}$ with probability at least $1-2\delta$

results.notes: Universal constant C absorbed into O notation. Conditional result based on an unverifiable eigenvalue assumption; R in the condition is undefined in the paper. Probability 1-2delta.
